title: Toolbar folder-delete silently drops the 'move presets to parent' option the context menu offers
existing_state: Deleting a folder from the tree's context menu (ctxDeleteFolder_Click, Form1.cs:8115-8188) presents a Yes/No/Cancel choice: Yes = delete folder AND presets, No = delete folder but move presets to the parent (8140-8153). The toolbar delete button (tsbDeleteFolder_Click, 8196-8239) performs the same operation but only offers a Yes/No 'delete folder and ALL its contents' confirmation (8222-8224) — always passing deletePresets: true (8232). A user trained by the context menu to expect a 'keep my presets' escape hatch loses it depending on which button they happened to click, and the only difference in safeguard is the dialog wording.
recommendation: Make tsbDeleteFolder_Click delegate to ctxDeleteFolder_Click (exactly as tsbAddFolder_Click already delegates to ctxAddFolder_Click at 8190-8194), after a small refactor so the shared handler resolves the selected folder node itself. One code path, one set of options, one fewer drift hazard.
user_benefit: Same action behaves the same everywhere; users keep the non-destructive 'move presets up' option regardless of entry point.

evidence.note: context menu: Yes=delete presets, No=move to parent, Cancel
tsbAddFolder already delegates to the context handler — the pattern exists
